title: Few-Shot Accent Synthesis for ASR with LLM-Guided Phoneme Editing
summary: Accented automatic speech recognition (ASR) often degrades due to the limited availability of accented training data. Prior work has explored accent modeling in low-resource settings, but existing approaches typically require minutes to hours of labeled speech, which may still be impractical for truly scarce accent scenarios. We propose a pipeline that adapts a text-to-speech (TTS) decoder to a target-accent speaker using fewer than ten reference utterances and employs large language model (LLM)-based phoneme editing to generate accent-conditioned pronunciations. The resulting synthetic speech is used to fine-tune a self-supervised ASR model. Experiments demonstrate consistent word error rate (WER) reductions on real accented speech, including cross-speaker evaluation and ultra-low data regimes. A matched-rate random phoneme baseline shows that phoneme-space perturbation itself is a strong form of augmentation, while LLM-guided edits provide additional gains through accent-conditioned structure.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a pipeline that adapts a TTS decoder to a target accent using fewer than ten utterances and uses LLM-based phoneme editing to generate accent-conditioned synthetic speech for fine-tuning a self-supervised ASR model, achieving consistent WER reductions in low-resource accent scenarios.
AI.motivation: Accented ASR performance degrades due to limited availability of accented training data; existing approaches require minutes to hours of labeled speech, which is impractical for truly scarce accent scenarios.
AI.method: Proposes a pipeline that: (1) adapts a TTS decoder to a target-accent speaker using fewer than ten reference utterances, (2) employs LLM-based phoneme editing to generate accent-conditioned pronunciations, (3) uses synthetic speech to fine-tune a self-supervised ASR model.
AI.result: Consistent WER reductions on real accented speech, including cross-speaker evaluation and ultra-low data regimes. Phoneme-space perturbation is a strong augmentation form, and LLM-guided edits provide additional gains through accent-conditioned structure.
AI.conclusion: The proposed pipeline effectively improves accented ASR in ultra-low-resource settings, with both random phoneme perturbation and LLM-guided editing contributing to performance gains.

title: Predicting Upcoming Stuttering Events from Three-Second Audio: Stratified Evaluation Reveals Severity-Selective Precursors, and the Model Deploys Fully On-Device
comment: 8 pages, 4 figures, 9 tables. Submitted to IEEE/ACM Transactions on Audio, Speech, and Language Processing
summary:
Audio-based stuttering systems to date have been trained for detection -- what disfluency is present now -- leaving prediction, the capability needed for closed-loop intervention, unstudied at deployable scale. We train a 616K-parameter CNN on SEP-28k (Apple, 20,131 three-second clips) to predict whether the next contiguous clip contains any disfluency.
  (1) Severity-selective precursor signal: on the episode-grouped test set, aggregate preblock AUC is modest (0.581 [0.542, 0.619]), but stratifying by upcoming event type reveals concentration on clinically severe events -- blocks 0.601 [0.554, 0.651] and sound repetitions 0.617 [0.567, 0.667] both exclude chance, while fillers (0.45) and word repetitions (0.49) are at chance. The aggregate objective converges to a severity-selective predictor because severe events carry prosodic precursors; fillers do not.
  (2) Cross-population transfer: without fine-tuning, the same checkpoint applied to 1,024 pediatric Children-Who-Stutter utterances (FluencyBank Teaching) attains AUC 0.674 detection and 0.655 prediction; DisfluencySpeech and LibriStutter reach 0.58-0.60 AUC.
  (3) Deployable on-device: lossless export to CoreML (1.19 MB), ONNX (40 KB), TFLite. Neural-Engine latency per 3 s window: 0.25 ms (iPhone 17 Pro Max, A19 Pro) to 0.55 ms (iPhone SE 3rd-gen and M1 Max). A 4 Hz streaming simulation uses 0.54% of the real-time budget. Platt-calibrated outputs (test ECE 0.010, from 0.177 raw).
  Five negative ablations -- output-level Future-Guided Learning, multi-clip GRU, time-axis concatenation, asymmetric focal loss, direct block-targeted training -- none improved over the vanilla baseline.

AI.tldr: A 616K-parameter CNN trained on SEP-28k predicts stuttering disfluencies in upcoming audio clips, achieving severity-selective prediction (AUC 0.601–0.617 for blocks/sound repetitions), cross-population transfer (AUC 0.674 detection, 0.655 prediction on pediatric data), and deployable on-device efficiency (0.25–0.55 ms latency, 0.54% real-time budget). Five ablations failed to improve the vanilla baseline.
AI.motivation: Prior audio-based stuttering systems focus only on detection (identifying current disfluency), leaving prediction unstudied at scale. Prediction is essential for closed-loop intervention systems.
AI.method: A 616K-parameter CNN trained on 20,131 three-second clips (SEP-28k) to predict disfluency in the next contiguous clip. Evaluated with severity-selective analysis, cross-population transfer to pediatric and other datasets, on-device deployment via CoreML/ONNX/TFLite, and five negative ablations.
AI.result: Aggregate preblock AUC 0.581; blocks 0.601, sound repetitions 0.617 (above chance), fillers 0.45 and word repetitions 0.49 (chance). Cross-population: pediatric AUC 0.674/0.655; others 0.58–0.60. On-device latency: 0.25–0.55 ms/3s window; 0.54% real-time budget. Platt-calibrated ECE 0.010. All five ablations failed to improve baseline.
AI.conclusion: Prediction of stuttering disfluency is feasible at scale, but only for clinically severe events (blocks, sound repetitions) which carry prosodic precursors. The model is efficient enough for on-device deployment, and the vanilla CNN baseline proved robust against all attempted ablations.

title: Accent Conversion: A Problem-Driven Survey of Sociolinguistic and Technical Constraints
summary: Accent conversion has rapidly progressed alongside growing interest in improving global cross-cultural communication. This survey presents an overview of the evolution of accent conversion methodologies, analyzing how the field has developed in response to fundamental challenges related to data alignment, representation disentanglement, and resource scarcity. We trace the progression from early rule-based digital signal processing approaches such as spectral manipulation and formant-based analysis to modern neural architectures capable of flexible and reference-free accent transformation. In addition, the survey situates accent conversion within its linguistic foundations and examines how different application requirements impose varying constraints on the balance between accent modification and speaker identity preservation. Finally, it reviews commonly used speech datasets and evaluation methodologies, identifies persistent challenges, and outlines directions for future research aimed at achieving more controllable and perceptually consistent accent conversion.

AI.tldr: This survey reviews accent conversion evolution from early rule-based DSP methods (spectral manipulation, formant analysis) to modern neural architectures enabling flexible, reference-free transformation. It covers challenges in data alignment, representation disentanglement, resource scarcity, and the trade-off between accent modification and speaker identity preservation, while reviewing datasets, evaluation methods, and future research directions.
AI.motivation: Growing interest in improving global cross-cultural communication drives the need for accent conversion technology.
AI.method: The survey traces the progression from early rule-based digital signal processing approaches (spectral manipulation, formant-based analysis) to modern neural architectures capable of flexible and reference-free accent transformation. It examines linguistic foundations and application requirements.
AI.result: Identified fundamental challenges: data alignment, representation disentanglement, and resource scarcity. Highlighted the trade-off between accent modification and speaker identity preservation across different application requirements.
AI.conclusion: Reviews speech datasets and evaluation methodologies, identifies persistent challenges, and outlines future research directions toward more controllable and perceptually consistent accent conversion.

title: LRS-VoxMM: A benchmark for in-the-wild audio-visual speech recognition
comment: Technical report for the LRS-VoxMM dataset release. Project page: https://mm.kaist.ac.kr/projects/voxmm
summary: We introduce LRS-VoxMM, an in-the-wild benchmark for audio-visual speech recognition (AVSR). The benchmark is derived from VoxMM, a dataset of diverse real-world spoken conversations with human-annotated transcriptions. We select AVSR-suitable samples and preprocess them in an LRS-style format for direct use in existing AVSR pipelines. Compared with commonly used benchmarks, LRS-VoxMM covers a more diverse range of scenarios and acoustic conditions. We also release distorted evaluation sets with additive noise, reverberation, and bandwidth limitation to support evaluation under severe acoustic degradation. Experimental results show that LRS-VoxMM is considerably harder than LRS3 and that the contribution of visual information becomes more evident as the audio signal degrades. LRS-VoxMM supports more realistic AVSR benchmarking and encourages further research on the role of visual information in challenging real-world conditions.

AI.tldr: LRS-VoxMM is a new in-the-wild AVSR benchmark derived from VoxMM, offering more diverse scenarios and acoustic conditions than LRS3, with distorted evaluation sets showing that visual information becomes more beneficial under audio degradation.
AI.motivation: Existing AVSR benchmarks like LRS3 lack diversity in real-world scenarios and acoustic conditions, motivating the need for a more challenging and realistic benchmark derived from in-the-wild conversations.
AI.method: The benchmark is derived from VoxMM, selecting AVSR-suitable samples and preprocessing them in an LRS-style format. Distorted evaluation sets with additive noise, reverberation, and bandwidth limitation are also released.
AI.result: LRS-VoxMM is considerably harder than LRS3, and the contribution of visual information becomes more evident as the audio signal degrades.
AI.conclusion: LRS-VoxMM supports more realistic AVSR benchmarking and encourages further research on the role of visual information in challenging real-world conditions.

title: Multidisciplinary Design Optimization for Wave-Driven Desalination Systems
summary: Wave-driven desalination systems are an innovative solution to the global freshwater crisis, leveraging the complementary characteristics of seawater reverse osmosis and wave energy converters. However, the high costs of this system pose a significant barrier to widespread adoption. Optimization can help these systems reach a more competitive levelized cost of water, but the highly coupled nature of the system necessitates a multidisciplinary design optimization approach. This paper presents a holistic, multidisciplinary design optimization framework for wave-driven desalination system design, integrating models for wave energy converter hydrodynamics, power take-off transmission, seawater reverse osmosis constraints, and economic analysis. This study demonstrates the impact of multidisciplinary design optimization for wave-driven desalination systems, resulting in a 69.5% reduction in levelized cost of water compared to a nominal design. We demonstrate that multidisciplinary design optimization outperforms sequential design approaches, yielding lower levelized costs of water and substantially different optimal designs. The multidisciplinary design optimization results suggest major design changes compared to designs found in the literature. Notably, smaller wave energy converters and larger pistons, along with smaller accumulators and larger seawater reverse osmosis plant installations, are preferred. These design trends are consistent across a range of sea states, suggesting potential generalizability beyond a single location. This study demonstrates the importance of holistic modeling and co-design for wave-driven desalination systems and establishes an effective optimization framework for future studies to build upon.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a multidisciplinary design optimization framework for wave-driven desalination systems, achieving a 69.5% reduction in levelized cost of water compared to nominal designs, and demonstrating that holistic co-design outperforms sequential approaches.
AI.motivation: Wave-driven desalination systems offer a solution to the global freshwater crisis by combining seawater reverse osmosis with wave energy converters, but high costs hinder widespread adoption. The highly coupled nature of the system necessitates a multidisciplinary design optimization approach to achieve competitive levelized cost of water.
AI.method: The authors developed a holistic, multidisciplinary design optimization framework integrating models for wave energy converter hydrodynamics, power take-off transmission, seawater reverse osmosis constraints, and economic analysis.
AI.result: The framework achieved a 69.5% reduction in levelized cost of water compared to a nominal design. Multidisciplinary design optimization outperformed sequential design approaches, yielding lower costs and substantially different optimal designs. Preferred designs included smaller wave energy converters, larger pistons, smaller accumulators, and larger seawater reverse osmosis plants.
AI.conclusion: Holistic modeling and co-design are critical for wave-driven desalination systems. The established optimization framework is effective and can serve as a foundation for future studies. Design trends are consistent across a range of sea states, suggesting generalizability beyond a single location.

title: A Knowledge-Driven Approach to Target Speech Extraction in the Presence of Background Sound Effects for Cinematic Audio Source Separation (CASS)
summary: We propose a knowledge-driven approach to speech target extraction in the presence of background sound effects already recorded in cinematic audio. The specific knowledge sources studied are manners of articulation that are detected in speech frames and adopted to form a knowledge vector as a part of features to enhance speech separation and target speech extraction because some short speech segments are often difficult to separate from mixed background sounds. Testing on the recent Sound Demixing Challenge data for cinematic audio source separation (CASS) shows that utilizing articulator-aware knowledge sources produces better separation results than those obtained without using any knowledge, especially for speech segments buried in unspecified background sound events.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a knowledge-driven approach for speech target extraction in cinematic audio by using articulatory features (manners of articulation) as additional knowledge vectors to improve speech separation, particularly for short speech segments mixed with background sounds. Tests on the CASS dataset show improved separation performance compared to not using such knowledge.
AI.motivation: Short speech segments in cinematic audio are often difficult to separate from mixed background sounds, motivating the need for additional knowledge sources to enhance speech separation and target extraction.
AI.method: The authors detect manners of articulation in speech frames and use them to form a knowledge vector as part of the feature set to enhance speech separation and target speech extraction in cinematic audio with background sound effects.
AI.result: Testing on the Sound Demixing Challenge data for cinematic audio source separation (CASS) shows that using articulator-aware knowledge sources yields better separation results compared to not using any knowledge, especially for speech segments buried in unspecified background sound events.
AI.conclusion: Incorporating articulatory knowledge (manners of articulation) as features improves speech separation performance in cinematic audio, particularly for challenging speech segments obscured by background sounds.

title: Learning to Spend: Model Predictive Control for Budgeting under Non-Stationary Returns
summary: We study finite-horizon budget allocation as a closed-loop economic control problem and evaluate receding-horizon Model Predictive Control (MPC) relative to reactive budgeting policies. Budgets are allocated periodically under execution noise and operational constraints, while return efficiency may evolve over time. Using a controlled simulation framework motivated by digital marketing, we compare reactive pacing to MPC across environments with increasing degrees of non-stationarity. Our results show that non-stationarity alone does not justify predictive control. When return dynamics are stationary or evolve through unpredictable stochastic drift, MPC offers no systematic advantage over reactive baselines. By contrast, when return efficiency exhibits predictable structure over the planning horizon, that is captured through an underlying model, MPC consistently outperforms reactive budgeting by exploiting intertemporal trade-offs.

AI.tldr: The paper studies finite-horizon budget allocation as a closed-loop control problem, comparing Model Predictive Control (MPC) to reactive budgeting policies. Using a digital marketing simulation, they find that MPC only outperforms reactive baselines when return efficiency exhibits predictable structure that can be modeled; under stationary or unpredictable stochastic drift, MPC offers no systematic advantage.
AI.motivation: To determine whether predictive control (MPC) offers advantages over reactive budgeting policies for finite-horizon budget allocation under non-stationarity, execution noise, and operational constraints.
AI.method: Formulate budget allocation as a closed-loop economic control problem; compare receding-horizon MPC to reactive pacing policies using a controlled simulation framework motivated by digital marketing, across environments with varying degrees of non-stationarity.
AI.result: MPC provides no systematic advantage over reactive baselines when return dynamics are stationary or evolve via unpredictable stochastic drift. MPC consistently outperforms reactive budgeting only when return efficiency exhibits predictable structure over the planning horizon captured by an underlying model.
AI.conclusion: Non-stationarity alone does not justify predictive control; the key condition for MPC's superiority is the presence of predictable structure in return dynamics that can be exploited for intertemporal trade-offs.

title: BUT System Description for CHiME-9 MCoRec Challenge
comment: Accepted to HSCMA 2026 Workshop at ICASSP 2026
summary: Multi-talker automatic speech recognition (ASR) in conversational recordings remains an open problem, particularly in scenarios with large portion of overlapping speech where identifying and transcribing a target speaker is difficult from audio alone. Visual cues can help resolve speaker ambiguity, yet their integration into long-context audio-visual (AV) ASR systems has been limited. The CHiME-9 MCoRec task addresses this challenge by requiring transcription of audio-visual recordings of heavily-overlapped parallel conversations, followed by clustering the participants into conversational groups. In this work, we present the BUT system based on a long-context target-speaker AV-ASR model capable of processing long-form recordings in a single decoding pass. Our architecture conditions a pre-trained NVIDIA Parakeet-v2 ASR model on visual representations from a pre-trained AV-HuBERT model. To cluster participants into conversation groups, we employ Qwen3.5-122B LLM to estimate transcript topic similarity followed by hierarchical agglomerative clustering. On the MCoRec development set, the proposed system achieves 33.7% WER and a clustering F1 score of 0.97, improving over the official baseline by 16.2% WER and 0.15 F1 absolute. On the eval set, our team ranked second, being 0.16% WER and 0.5% F1 worse than the best system.

AI.tldr: The BUT system for the CHiME-9 MCoRec task uses a long-context target-speaker audio-visual ASR model (conditioning Parakeet-v2 on AV-HuBERT visual features) and LLM-based topic clustering (Qwen3.5-122B + hierarchical agglomerative clustering), achieving 33.7% WER and 0.97 F1 on the dev set, ranking second on the eval set.
AI.motivation: Multi-talker ASR in conversational recordings with heavy overlap remains unsolved; visual cues can help resolve speaker ambiguity but their integration into long-context AV-ASR systems has been limited.
AI.method: A long-context target-speaker AV-ASR model conditioning a pre-trained NVIDIA Parakeet-v2 ASR model on visual representations from a pre-trained AV-HuBERT model, processing long-form recordings in a single decoding pass; conversation clustering via Qwen3.5-122B LLM for topic similarity estimation followed by hierarchical agglomerative clustering.
AI.result: 33.7% WER and 0.97 clustering F1 on the MCoRec development set, improving over the official baseline by 16.2% WER and 0.15 F1; ranked second on the eval set within 0.16% WER and 0.5% F1 of the best system.
AI.conclusion: The proposed AV-ASR system effectively handles heavily-overlapped conversational recordings with visual speaker disambiguation and LLM-based clustering, achieving competitive performance on the CHiME-9 MCoRec task.

title: Regime-Adaptive Weighted Ensemble Learning for Computing-Driven Dynamic Load Forecasting in AI Data Centers
summary: Short-term load forecasting for AI data centers presents new challenges because it is computing-driven, with heterogeneous job arrivals, sizes, and durations exhibiting bursty, non-stationary dynamics. Compared with traditional load types, data center loads are less researched and can pose greater threats to the efficiency and stability of power grids. To close the gap, this paper proposes a regime-adaptive ensemble learning forecasting algorithm to predict computing-driven dynamic workloads in AI data centers. A weight-learned neural network within an ensemble learning framework is developed to exploit the complementary strengths of two machine learning (ML) submodels across varying operating regimes. Furthermore, a novel feature engineering strategy is developed to incrementally learn from a non-stationary data stream. Thus, the ensemble weights are dynamically optimized to facilitate adaptive calibration of inter-submodel contributions. Comparative case studies on the MIT Supercloud dataset demonstrate that the proposed method significantly enhances load forecasting accuracy and adaptivity across various regimes, and the selected combination of ML models for ensemble learning outperforms other possible combinations. To the best of our knowledge, our method is the first to reduce minute-class forecasting errors for AI data center loads to below 1%, highlighting its potential for grid-interactive coordination and demand response.

AI.tldr: Proposes a regime-adaptive ensemble learning method for short-term load forecasting in AI data centers, achieving sub-1% minute-level prediction errors on the MIT Supercloud dataset.
AI.motivation: AI data center loads are computing-driven with bursty, non-stationary dynamics (heterogeneous job arrivals, sizes, durations), posing greater threats to grid efficiency and stability compared to traditional loads, yet they are under-researched.
AI.method: A regime-adaptive ensemble learning algorithm with (1) a weight-learned neural network that combines two ML submodels, (2) a feature engineering strategy for incremental learning from non-stationary data streams, and (3) dynamically optimized ensemble weights for adaptive calibration across operating regimes.
AI.result: On the MIT Supercloud dataset, the method significantly improves forecasting accuracy and adaptivity across regimes; it is the first to reduce minute-class forecasting errors for AI data center loads below 1%.
AI.conclusion: The proposed method effectively addresses the unique challenges of AI data center load forecasting, enabling better grid-interactive coordination and demand response.

title: Feedback Linearization of Hyperbolic PDEs with Volterra Nonlinearities
summary:
Alberto Isidori's framework of geometric nonlinear control, and particularly of feedback linearization, is the inspiration behind PDE backstepping: apply a transfromation of the state to cast the plant into a canonical form, bring all the non-canonical effects within the "span" of (boundary) control, and close the design with a feedback that makes the closed loop evolve in accordance with well-studied stable dynamics. The specificity of this approach is that, for PDEs, there is not one canonical form (like Brunovsky for ODEs) but the canonical forms are PDE-class-specific. When conducting this process for nonlinear PDEs, where the "transformation of the state" is performed using a nonlinear Volterra series indexed by the spatial variable, enormous technical challenges arise. One has to deal with kernels governed by PDEs on simplex domains growing in dimension to infinity, capture the growth rates of these kernels of the "direct transformation," and conduct the same for the "inverse transformation" without directly studying its Volterra kernels. So far, this agenda has been executed only once, two decades ago: for parabolic PDEs by Vazquez and Krstic [Automatica, 2008]. Generalization attempts have not followed because of the immense complexity involved in feedback-linearizing nonlinear PDEs.
  In this paper, dedicated to Professor Isidori, we convert the PDE feedback-linearizing methodology of 2008 from the parabolic to a hyperbolic class and, for a transport-adapted subclass of Chen-Fliess series, construct controllers without kernel PDEs.

AI.tldr: This paper extends PDE feedback linearization from parabolic to hyperbolic systems, adapting the Volterra-series-based methodology to a transport-adapted subclass of Chen-Fliess series, thereby avoiding kernel PDEs entirely.
AI.motivation: Motivated by the enormous technical challenges in generalizing nonlinear PDE feedback linearization beyond the parabolic case (only achieved once, two decades ago), the authors aim to convert the methodology to hyperbolic systems and simplify it by eliminating kernel PDEs.
AI.method: The method adapts the PDE feedback-linearizing framework (inspired by Isidori's geometric nonlinear control) from parabolic to hyperbolic PDEs, using nonlinear Volterra series indexed by spatial variables, and for a transport-adapted subclass of Chen-Fliess series, constructs controllers without requiring kernel PDEs.
AI.result: Successful conversion of the feedback-linearizing methodology from parabolic to hyperbolic PDE class, and derivation of controllers free of kernel PDEs for a specific transport-adapted subclass of Chen-Fliess series.
AI.conclusion: The paper demonstrates that the PDE feedback linearization agenda can be extended beyond parabolic systems, and that for certain hyperbolic subclasses the complexity can be drastically reduced by eliminating kernel PDEs, opening new avenues for nonlinear PDE control.

title: Robust Geometric Control of Catenary Robots under Unstructured Force Uncertainties
summary: This paper considers the robust control of a catenary robot composed of two quadrotors connected by an inextensible cable. The system is modeled on \(SE(3)\), with the cable treated as a geometric subsystem induced by the UAV configuration rather than as an independent dynamical element. The catenary shape determines configuration-dependent forces that couple the translational dynamics of the vehicles. We propose a geometric tracking controller for the relative configuration of the agents and analyze its robustness with respect to unstructured uncertainties in the catenary-induced forces. The main theoretical result establishes local input-to-state stability of the closed-loop tracking errors. In particular, we obtain asymptotic convergence in the nominal case and an explicit ultimate bound for the tracking errors under bounded catenary-force perturbations.

AI.tldr: The paper presents a robust geometric controller for a dual-quadrotor catenary robot system on SE(3), treating the cable as a geometric constraint rather than a dynamic element, and proves local input-to-state stability with asymptotic convergence in the nominal case and bounded errors under perturbations.
AI.motivation: To develop a robust control framework for catenary robots (two quadrotors connected by an inextensible cable) that accounts for configuration-dependent coupling forces induced by the cable shape, and to provide formal stability guarantees under model uncertainties.
AI.method: The system is modeled on SE(3) with the cable treated as a geometric subsystem induced by UAV configuration. A geometric tracking controller for the relative configuration of the agents is proposed. Robustness analysis uses input-to-state stability (ISS) framework with respect to unstructured uncertainties in catenary-induced forces.
AI.result: Local input-to-state stability of closed-loop tracking errors is established. Asymptotic convergence is achieved in the nominal (unperturbed) case. An explicit ultimate bound for tracking errors under bounded catenary-force perturbations is derived.
AI.conclusion: The proposed geometric controller ensures robust tracking performance for the catenary robot system, with formal stability guarantees that hold even when the catenary-induced forces are subject to unstructured uncertainties.

title: Optimal Functional Incentives for Control: The Linear-Quadratic Case with Bilinear Incentives
summary: We study the design of functional incentive mechanisms for dynamical systems, in which a leader designs a fixed incentive function to motivate a self-interested follower to actuate the system beneficially over an extended horizon, without real-time revision of the incentive. This stands in contrast to the adaptive paradigm, in which the incentive is itself a continuously updated control variable. We formalize the problem as a discrete-time bi-level optimal control problem and derive analytical results for the linear-quadratic case with bilinear incentives and a myopic follower. Specifically, we establish a necessary and sufficient stability condition for the induced closed-loop system, derive a closed-form expression for the gradient of the expected leader cost with respect to the incentive parameter matrix, and obtain a fully closed-form cost expression in the scalar setting. Based on the latter, explicit characterizations of the optimal incentive parameter are provided in two asymptotic regimes: the infinite-horizon limit and the limit of high follower cost. For long horizons, the optimal incentive is shown to become independent of the follower's private cost parameter, with direct implications for robust mechanism design under private information.

AI.tldr: This paper studies fixed incentive mechanisms for dynamical systems where a leader designs a static incentive function to influence a self-interested follower's behavior over an extended horizon, without real-time adjustments. It formalizes the problem as a bi-level optimal control problem, provides analytical results for linear-quadratic systems with bilinear incentives and myopic followers, including stability conditions, closed-form gradient and cost expressions, and optimal incentive characterizations in asymptotic regimes.
AI.motivation: To move beyond adaptive (real-time updated) incentive paradigms and study fixed incentive mechanisms that can be designed once and deployed over long horizons, which is more practical in many real-world settings where continuous revision of incentives is infeasible or costly.
AI.method: The problem is formalized as a discrete-time bi-level optimal control problem. Analytical derivations focus on the linear-quadratic case with bilinear incentives and a myopic follower, including stability analysis, gradient computation via closed-form expressions, and asymptotic analysis in the infinite-horizon and high-follower-cost limits.
AI.result: A necessary and sufficient stability condition for the induced closed-loop system is established. A closed-form expression for the gradient of the expected leader cost w.r.t. the incentive parameter matrix is derived. A fully closed-form cost expression is obtained in the scalar setting. In the infinite-horizon limit, the optimal incentive becomes independent of the follower's private cost parameter.
AI.conclusion: The optimal incentive's asymptotic independence from the follower's private cost parameter has direct implications for robust mechanism design under private information, suggesting that fixed incentives can be effective even without knowing the follower's exact cost structure.

title: On the Nesterov's acceleration: A NAIM perspective
summary: We present a unifying Nearly Asymptotically Invariant Manifold (NAIM) framework for understanding Nesterovs Accelerated Gradient (NAG) method. By lifting the first-order gradient flow into a second-order phase space we construct a NAIM a slow, attracting graph and show that acceleration emerges from a curvature aware perturbation of this graph. The evolving slope of the perturbed manifold is governed by a Differential Riccati Equation (DRE), which enforces strict tangency of the vector field to the manifold surface. In the quadratic case the DRE reduces to an Algebraic Riccati Equation (ARE), and the requirement of spectral resonance equal contraction rates across all curvature modes uniquely determines the damping coefficient, directly yielding the continuous time Nesterov ODE. Fenichels theorem then extends this picture rigorously to general smooth, strongly convex landscapes: normal hyperbolicity guarantees persistence of the accelerated manifold despite varying Hessian curvature. The method is further extended to unified geometric derivation of NAG methods for smooth convex and strongly convex optimization in the discrete case. We exploit the underlying geometric structure and derive both cases from the same principle of preserving the projective structure under discretization process. A Lie Trotter splitting separates the linear dissipative dynamics from the nonlinear gradient flow. The dissipative subsystem is integrated by the Cayley (bilinear) transform, which preserves the underlying projective (Mobius) structure unconditionally and produces the classical Nesterov momentum coefficient as the unique Pade multiplier. For the convex case, projective flatness (vanishing Schwarzian derivative) uniquely selects the time-varying damping recovering the canonical Nesterov ODE for convex functions.

AI.tldr: A unified geometric framework (NAIM) explains Nesterov Accelerated Gradient via second-order phase space lifting, Differential Riccati Equations, spectral resonance, and Lie-Trotter splitting with Cayley transforms, recovering classical Nesterov ODEs and momentum coefficients for both convex and strongly convex settings.
AI.motivation: To provide a unifying geometric explanation for why Nesterov's Accelerated Gradient method works, bridging continuous-time dynamical systems and discrete optimization through invariant manifold theory.
AI.method: Lifts first-order gradient flow into second-order phase space; constructs Nearly Asymptotically Invariant Manifold (NAIM); uses Differential Riccati Equation (DRE) to enforce tangency; applies Fenichel's theorem for persistence; uses Lie-Trotter splitting and Cayley transform for discretization.
AI.result: In quadratic case, DRE reduces to ARE and spectral resonance uniquely determines damping, yielding continuous-time Nesterov ODE. For convex case, projective flatness (vanishing Schwarzian derivative) uniquely selects time-varying damping. Cayley transform produces classical Nesterov momentum coefficient as unique Padé multiplier.
AI.conclusion: The NAIM framework provides a rigorous geometric unification of Nesterov acceleration for both smooth convex and strongly convex optimization in continuous and discrete time.

title: A MEC-Based Optimization Framework for Dynamic Inductive Charging
comment: Accepted for publication at IEEE Vehicular Networking Conference (VNC) 2026, Montreal, Canada, June 2026
summary: Range anxiety and long recharging times remain critical barriers to electric vehicle adoption. Dynamic Inductive Charging (DIC) offers a compelling solution by enabling wireless power transfer while driving, potentially reducing battery size requirements and thus vehicle costs. However, DIC infrastructures are expensive and power-constrained, requiring intelligent resource allocation to maximize user satisfaction and economic viability. We propose a Model Predictive Control framework for optimal power allocation in DIC systems, using edge computing and vehicular communications to prioritize vehicles with critical battery states. The framework is implemented and evaluated through SUMO-based simulations on a realistic 10 km urban scenario in Istanbul, Turkey, under varying traffic intensities. Results demonstrate two critical limitations of uncoordinated allocation. First, resource utilization remains suboptimal despite available power when demand saturates system capacity. Second, when demand exceeds capacity, uniform distribution of power leaves a heavy tail of critically unsatisfied vehicles that may require emergency stops. Our MPC-based strategy addresses both regimes -- maximizing power utilization during saturation through dynamic stripe rebalancing, and improving satisfaction fairness under scarcity by aggressively prioritizing depleted batteries at the expense of well-charged vehicles. The framework and simulation tools are released as open-source to support further research in this emerging domain.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a Model Predictive Control (MPC) framework for optimal power allocation in Dynamic Inductive Charging systems for electric vehicles. Using SUMO simulations of a 10 km urban scenario in Istanbul, the approach addresses two key limitations of uncoordinated allocation: suboptimal resource utilization under demand saturation, and unfair satisfaction distribution under demand exceeding capacity. The MPC strategy dynamically rebalances power allocation, prioritizing critically depleted batteries.
AI.motivation: Range anxiety and long recharging times are critical barriers to EV adoption. DIC systems offer a solution but are expensive and power-constrained, requiring intelligent resource allocation to maximize user satisfaction and economic viability.
AI.method: A Model Predictive Control (MPC) framework for optimal power allocation, leveraging edge computing and vehicular communications. Evaluated via SUMO-based simulations on a realistic 10 km urban scenario in Istanbul under varying traffic intensities.
AI.result: Uncoordinated allocation has two critical limitations: (1) suboptimal resource utilization despite available power under demand saturation, and (2) a heavy tail of critically unsatisfied vehicles under demand exceeding capacity. The MPC strategy maximizes power utilization during saturation via dynamic stripe rebalancing and improves satisfaction fairness under scarcity by aggressively prioritizing depleted batteries.
AI.conclusion: The MPC-based strategy outperforms uncoordinated allocation in both regimes. The framework and simulation tools are released as open-source to support further research.

title: Intelligent Self-tuning Active EMI Filtering for Electrified Automotive Power Systems Using Reinforcement Learning
summary: The rapid electrification and intelligence of modern transportation systems place stringent demands on the electromagnetic compatibility, reliability, and adaptability of automotive power electronics. In electric and autonomous vehicles, electromagnetic interference (EMI) generated by high-frequency switching power converters can compromise safety-critical functions, in-vehicle communications, and system efficiency under dynamic operating conditions. Conventional passive EMI filters, while robust, are often oversized and lack adaptability, leading to increased weight, volume, and energy losses. This paper proposes an intelligent self-tuning active EMI filtering approach for electrified automotive power systems based on reinforcement learning (RL). The EMI mitigation problem is formulated as a Markov decision process, enabling an RL agent to continuously adapt filter parameters in response to time-varying interference characteristics. To improve robustness and generalisation under complex and non-stationary conditions, a variational autoencoder is employed for compact state representation, while a noise-based exploration mechanism enhances learning efficiency and prevents suboptimal convergence. The proposed method is evaluated using experimentally measured EMI spectra from an automotive electric drive unit within a MATLAB/Simulink co-simulation framework. Results demonstrate consistent EMI attenuation improvements of 25-30 dB across a wide frequency range compared with conventional control strategies and passive filtering solutions. By reducing reliance on oversized passive components and enabling adaptive EMI suppression, the proposed framework supports lightweight, energy-efficient, and reliable power-electronic systems for intelligent and green transportation applications.

AI.tldr: An RL-based active EMI filter with VAE state representation and noise-based exploration achieves 25-30 dB attenuation improvement over conventional passive filters in automotive power electronics.
AI.motivation: Conventional passive EMI filters in automotive power electronics are oversized, lack adaptability, and cause increased weight, volume, and energy losses, failing to meet the stringent EMC demands of electrified and autonomous vehicles under dynamic operating conditions.
AI.method: The EMI mitigation problem is formulated as a Markov decision process; an RL agent continuously adapts filter parameters; a variational autoencoder (VAE) compacts the state representation; a noise-based exploration mechanism enhances learning and prevents suboptimal convergence; evaluated using experimental EMI spectra from an automotive e-drive unit in MATLAB/Simulink co-simulation.
AI.result: Consistent EMI attenuation improvements of 25-30 dB across a wide frequency range compared to conventional control strategies and passive filtering solutions.
AI.conclusion: The proposed RL-based adaptive EMI filter reduces reliance on oversized passive components, enabling lightweight, energy-efficient, and reliable power-electronic systems for intelligent and green transportation.

title: Hierarchical Control for Continuous-time Systems via General Approximate Alternating Simulation Relations
summary: This paper introduces a general approximate alternating simulation relation (\emph{$\varepsilon$-gAAS relation}) for continuous-time systems, which relaxes existing simulation relations to tolerate larger mismatches between abstract and concrete models. The definition of gAAS for continuous-time systems is first proposed, and its properties are investigated. Then, a control refinement method is developed to enable hierarchical control for the gAAS relation. Finally, case studies demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach, highlighting its advantages over existing methods.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces an ε-gAAS relation for continuous-time systems, which relaxes existing simulation relations to tolerate larger mismatches between abstract and concrete models. It proposes a control refinement method for hierarchical control and demonstrates effectiveness via case studies.
AI.motivation: To address the limitations of existing simulation relations that cannot tolerate sufficiently large mismatches between abstract and concrete continuous-time system models.
AI.method: The authors first define the ε-gAAS (general approximate alternating simulation) relation for continuous-time systems, investigate its properties, and then develop a control refinement method that enables hierarchical control based on this relaxed relation.
AI.result: Case studies demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed ε-gAAS relation and control refinement method, showing advantages over existing approaches.
AI.conclusion: The ε-gAAS relation successfully enables greater tolerance for model mismatches in continuous-time systems, facilitating more flexible hierarchical control.
